DOS Header.title: DOS Header (MZ Header)
DOS Header.description: The DOS header is the first structure in every PE file. It was originally designed for DOS compatibility but now serves as a legacy header that points to the actual PE header. The magic number 'MZ' (0x5A4D) identifies this as a valid executable file.
DOS Header.purpose: Provides backward compatibility and contains the offset to the PE header
DOS Header.security_notes: Legacy header - no direct security implications, but must be present for valid PE files

PE Header.title: PE Header (File Header)
PE Header.description: The PE header contains essential information about the file format, including the target machine type, number of sections, and characteristics. It follows the DOS header and contains the core PE format information.
PE Header.purpose: Define the basic PE file structure and characteristics
PE Header.security_notes: Critical for file validation - check Machine field for unexpected architectures and Characteristics for suspicious flags

Optional Header.title: Optional Header
Optional Header.description: The optional header contains detailed information about the executable, including entry point, image base, section alignment, and subsystem information. It's essential for the Windows loader to properly load and execute the file.
Optional Header.purpose: Provide detailed loading and execution information for the Windows loader
Optional Header.security_notes: Critical security fields include EntryPoint, ImageBase, and DllCharacteristics. Unusual values may indicate malicious modifications.

Sections.title: PE Sections
Sections.description: Sections contain the actual code, data, and resources of the executable. Each section has specific characteristics and permissions that determine how it's loaded into memory and what operations are allowed.
Sections.purpose: Organize executable content into logical, loadable segments with specific permissions
Sections.security_notes: Critical for security analysis - check section characteristics for suspicious permissions, look for hidden sections, and verify section alignment

Data Directories.title: Data Directories
Data Directories.description: Data directories point to important structures within the file, such as import/export tables, resources, and security information. They provide the loader with locations of critical data needed for execution.
Data Directories.purpose: Locate important data structures for loading and execution
Data Directories.security_notes: Import/Export directories are critical for security analysis. Check for suspicious imports, unexpected exports, and verify directory integrity

WIN_CERTIFICATE.title: WIN_CERTIFICATE (Attribute Certificate)
WIN_CERTIFICATE.description: Holds an Authenticode signature or other attribute certificate appended to the PE file. The Certificate Directory entry’s VirtualAddress field is a raw file offset to this structure (not an RVA). dwLength covers the whole record; wCertificateType is often 0x0002 (WIN_CERT_TYPE_PKCS_SIGNED_DATA) for PKCS#7 signed data.
WIN_CERTIFICATE.purpose: Code signing, integrity, and publisher identity for the image
WIN_CERTIFICATE.security_notes: Compare with catalog signatures on disk; stripped or mismatched certificates can indicate tampering. The payload in bCertificate is ASN.1 / PKCS#7 — use a dedicated tool to parse the full chain.

e_magic.title: Magic Number (e_magic)
e_magic.description: This 16-bit value must be 0x5A4D ('MZ' in ASCII). It's the signature that identifies this file as a valid DOS executable. The 'MZ' stands for Mark Zbikowski, one of the original DOS developers.
e_magic.security_notes: Critical validation field - any other value indicates file corruption or manipulation. Malware authors sometimes try to modify this to bypass basic file type detection.

e_cblp.title: Bytes on Last Page (e_cblp)
e_cblp.description: The number of bytes on the last page of the file. This field is used to determine the exact size of the file.
e_cblp.purpose: Calculate exact file size for DOS compatibility
e_cblp.security_notes: Unusual values might indicate file manipulation or padding.

e_cp.title: Pages in File (e_cp)
e_cp.description: The number of pages in the file. In DOS, files were organized in 512-byte pages.
e_cp.security_notes: Legacy field with minimal security implications.

e_crlc.title: Relocations (e_crlc)
e_crlc.description: The number of relocation entries in the file. These are used to adjust addresses when the file cannot be loaded at its preferred base address.
e_crlc.purpose: Handle address space conflicts in DOS
e_crlc.security_notes: High numbers might indicate complex relocations or manipulation.

e_cparhdr.title: Size of Header (e_cparhdr)
e_cparhdr.description: The size of the header in paragraphs (16-byte units). This includes the DOS header and any additional header information.
e_cparhdr.security_notes: Unusual header sizes might indicate header manipulation.

e_minalloc.title: Minimum Allocation (e_minalloc)
e_minalloc.description: The minimum number of paragraphs of memory that the program needs to run.
e_minalloc.security_notes: Very high values might indicate memory allocation attacks.

e_maxalloc.title: Maximum Allocation (e_maxalloc)
e_maxalloc.description: The maximum number of paragraphs of memory that the program can use.
e_maxalloc.security_notes: Unusually high values might indicate memory exhaustion attacks.

e_ss.title: Initial SS (e_ss)
e_ss.description: The initial value of the SS register (stack segment) when the program starts.
e_ss.security_notes: Unusual stack locations might indicate stack manipulation.

e_sp.title: Initial SP (e_sp)
e_sp.description: The initial value of the SP register (stack pointer) when the program starts.
e_sp.security_notes: Unusual stack pointers might indicate stack overflow attempts.

e_csum.title: Checksum (e_csum)
e_csum.description: A checksum value for the file. This field is often set to 0 in modern PE files.
e_csum.security_notes: Non-zero checksums should be validated. Zero is normal for modern files.

e_ip.title: Initial IP (e_ip)
e_ip.description: The initial value of the IP register (instruction pointer) when the program starts.
e_ip.security_notes: Unusual instruction pointers might indicate code injection.

e_cs.title: Initial CS (e_cs)
e_cs.description: The initial value of the CS register (code segment) when the program starts.
e_cs.security_notes: Unusual code segments might indicate segment manipulation.

e_lfarlc.title: File Address of Relocation Table (e_lfarlc)
e_lfarlc.description: The file address of the relocation table. This points to the relocation entries.
e_lfarlc.security_notes: Unusual relocation table locations might indicate manipulation.

e_ovno.title: Overlay Number (e_ovno)
e_ovno.description: The overlay number. This field is typically 0 for the main program.
e_ovno.security_notes: Non-zero values might indicate overlay-based malware.

e_lfanew.title: PE Header Offset (e_lfanew)
e_lfanew.description: This 32-bit value contains the file offset to the PE header. It tells the loader where to find the actual Portable Executable header within the file. This offset is typically 0x80 (128 bytes) or larger.
e_lfanew.purpose: Locate the PE header for modern Windows execution
e_lfanew.calculation: File offset from beginning of file to PE signature
e_lfanew.security_notes: Suspicious if offset is very large (>0x1000) - could indicate file padding to hide malicious content. Also check if offset points to valid PE signature.

DOS_STUB.title: DOS stub
DOS_STUB.description: This 64-byte region (when the PE signature is at 0x80) sits right after the 64-byte IMAGE_DOS_HEADER (0x00–0x3F). It is the MS-DOS stub: a small 16-bit real-mode program the linker embeds in the file. If someone runs the file under MS-DOS, the CPU executes this code; it typically prints a message such as “This program cannot be run in DOS mode” and exits. Under Windows, the loader ignores this path and uses e_lfanew at offset 0x3C to find the PE header (“PE\0\0”) instead. The bytes are 8086/8088 machine code and data — not another formal PE structure.
DOS_STUB.purpose: Legacy compatibility only; the stub runs only in a DOS environment. It fills the gap between the fixed DOS header and the PE block at e_lfanew.
DOS_STUB.note: Developers can replace the default stub with custom 16-bit code (e.g. CTF/crackme challenges) using the linker /STUB option or similar tools. If e_lfanew is less than 0x80, only part of 0x40–0x7F is stub; bytes from e_lfanew onward belong to the PE layout.
DOS_STUB.security_notes: Custom or packed stubs may differ from the default Microsoft message. Compare with known linkers; unusual stub size, entropy, or behavior can warrant deeper analysis.

Signature.title: PE Signature
Signature.description: The PE signature that identifies this as a valid Portable Executable file. Must be 0x00004550 ('PE\0\0' in ASCII).
Signature.security_notes: Critical validation field - any other value indicates file corruption or manipulation.

Machine.title: Machine Type
Machine.description: Specifies the target CPU architecture for this executable. Common values include: 0x014C (Intel 386), 0x8664 (AMD64), 0x01C0 (ARM), 0xAA64 (ARM64).
Machine.purpose: Ensure the executable runs on compatible hardware
Machine.security_notes: Check for architecture mismatch - running 64-bit malware on 32-bit system or vice versa. Some malware uses multiple architectures in single file.

NumberOfSections.title: Number of Sections
NumberOfSections.description: Indicates how many sections are defined in the section table. Each section represents a logical division of the executable (code, data, resources, etc.). Typical executables have 3-10 sections.
NumberOfSections.purpose: Define the file's logical structure and memory layout
NumberOfSections.security_notes: Suspicious if very few sections (<3) or too many (>15). Few sections might indicate packed/obfuscated code. Many sections could indicate code injection or complex malware.

TimeDateStamp.title: Time/Date Stamp
TimeDateStamp.description: Contains the timestamp when the executable was created or last modified. This is stored as seconds since January 1, 1970 (Unix epoch).
TimeDateStamp.security_notes: Check for suspicious timestamps: future dates, very old dates, or dates matching known malware campaigns. Timestamp manipulation is common in malware.

PointerToSymbolTable.title: Pointer to Symbol Table
PointerToSymbolTable.description: Points to the COFF symbol table. This is typically 0 in modern PE files as symbol information is usually stored in separate PDB files.
PointerToSymbolTable.security_notes: Non-zero values in release builds might indicate debug information left behind or manipulation.

NumberOfSymbols.title: Number of Symbols
NumberOfSymbols.description: The number of symbols in the COFF symbol table. This is typically 0 in modern PE files.
NumberOfSymbols.security_notes: Non-zero values in release builds might indicate debug information left behind or manipulation.

SizeOfOptionalHeader.title: Size of Optional Header
SizeOfOptionalHeader.description: The size of the optional header in bytes. This field indicates how much optional header data follows the PE header.
SizeOfOptionalHeader.security_notes: Unusual sizes might indicate header manipulation or corruption.

Characteristics.title: File Characteristics
Characteristics.description: A set of flags that describe the executable's properties: 0x0002 (Executable), 0x2000 (DLL), 0x0001 (Relocation info stripped), 0x0100 (32-bit word machine).
Characteristics.security_notes: DLL characteristics in EXE files are suspicious. Stripped relocation info can indicate packed malware. Check for unusual combinations of flags.

Magic.title: Magic Number
Magic.description: Identifies the type of optional header: 0x010B (PE32), 0x020B (PE32+).
Magic.security_notes: Must match file architecture. Mismatch could indicate file corruption or manipulation. Some malware tries to confuse analysis tools.

MajorLinkerVersion.title: Major Linker Version
MajorLinkerVersion.description: The major version of the linker that created this executable.
MajorLinkerVersion.security_notes: Very old or very new linker versions might indicate suspicious compilation or manipulation.

MinorLinkerVersion.title: Minor Linker Version
MinorLinkerVersion.description: The minor version of the linker that created this executable.
MinorLinkerVersion.security_notes: Very old or very new linker versions might indicate suspicious compilation or manipulation.

SizeOfCode.title: Size of Code
SizeOfCode.description: The size of the code section in bytes. This represents the total size of all code sections combined.
SizeOfCode.security_notes: Suspicious if very large or very small compared to file size. Could indicate code injection or obfuscation.

SizeOfInitializedData.title: Size of Initialized Data
SizeOfInitializedData.description: The size of the initialized data section in bytes. This includes all data sections that contain initialized values.
SizeOfInitializedData.security_notes: Unusual sizes might indicate data injection or manipulation.

SizeOfUninitializedData.title: Size of Uninitialized Data
SizeOfUninitializedData.description: The size of the uninitialized data section (BSS) in bytes. This section is filled with zeros at load time.
SizeOfUninitializedData.security_notes: Large BSS sections might indicate malware trying to allocate memory for unpacking or code injection.

AddressOfEntryPoint.title: Address of Entry Point
AddressOfEntryPoint.description: The relative virtual address (RVA) where execution begins when the program starts. This points to the first instruction that will be executed.
AddressOfEntryPoint.purpose: Define the starting point of program execution
AddressOfEntryPoint.security_notes: CRITICAL SECURITY FIELD! Suspicious if: 1) Points to data section (not code), 2) Very low address (<0x1000), 3) Points to last section, 4) Points to overlay. These often indicate packed malware or code injection.

BaseOfCode.title: Base of Code
BaseOfCode.description: The RVA of the beginning of the code section when loaded into memory.
BaseOfCode.security_notes: Unusual base addresses might indicate code injection or manipulation.

BaseOfData.title: Base of Data
BaseOfData.description: The RVA of the beginning of the data section when loaded into memory. This field is only present in PE32 files.
BaseOfData.security_notes: Unusual base addresses might indicate data injection or manipulation.

ImageBase.title: Image Base
ImageBase.description: The preferred base address in memory where the executable should be loaded. The default is 0x00400000 for 32-bit and 0x0000000140000000 for 64-bit executables.
ImageBase.purpose: Optimize memory layout and reduce relocation overhead
ImageBase.security_notes: Endereços base incomuns podem indicar malware tentando evitar detecção ou conflito com outros processos. Verifique valores não padrão.

SectionAlignment.title: Section Alignment
SectionAlignment.description: The alignment of sections in memory. Sections are aligned to this boundary when loaded into memory. Common values are 0x1000 (4KB) for 32-bit and 0x2000 (8KB) for 64-bit.
SectionAlignment.security_notes: Unusual alignment values might indicate manipulation or non-standard compilation.

FileAlignment.title: File Alignment
FileAlignment.description: The alignment of sections in the file. Raw data is aligned to this boundary on disk. Common values are 0x200 (512 bytes) or 0x1000 (4KB).
FileAlignment.security_notes: Unusual file alignment might indicate manipulation or non-standard compilation.

MajorOperatingSystemVersion.title: Major Operating System Version
MajorOperatingSystemVersion.description: The major version number of the operating system required to run this executable.
MajorOperatingSystemVersion.security_notes: Unusual OS version requirements might indicate targeted malware or compatibility issues.

MinorOperatingSystemVersion.title: Minor Operating System Version
MinorOperatingSystemVersion.description: The minor version number of the operating system required to run this executable.
MinorOperatingSystemVersion.security_notes: Unusual OS version requirements might indicate targeted malware or compatibility issues.

MajorImageVersion.title: Major Image Version
MajorImageVersion.description: The major version number of the image itself. This is typically set by the developer.
MajorImageVersion.security_notes: Unusual version numbers might indicate manipulation or fake versioning.

MinorImageVersion.title: Minor Image Version
MinorImageVersion.description: The minor version number of the image itself. This is typically set by the developer.
MinorImageVersion.security_notes: Unusual version numbers might indicate manipulation or fake versioning.

MajorSubsystemVersion.title: Major Subsystem Version
MajorSubsystemVersion.description: The major version number of the subsystem required to run this executable.
MajorSubsystemVersion.security_notes: Unusual subsystem version requirements might indicate compatibility issues or manipulation.

MinorSubsystemVersion.title: Minor Subsystem Version
MinorSubsystemVersion.description: The minor version number of the subsystem required to run this executable.
MinorSubsystemVersion.security_notes: Unusual subsystem version requirements might indicate compatibility issues or manipulation.

Win32VersionValue.title: Win32 Version Value
Win32VersionValue.description: Reserved field that should be 0. This field is not used by the Windows loader.
Win32VersionValue.security_notes: Non-zero values might indicate file corruption or non-standard PE format.

SizeOfImage.title: Size of Image
SizeOfImage.description: The total size of the image when loaded into memory, including all headers and sections.
SizeOfImage.security_notes: Unusual image sizes might indicate code injection or manipulation.

SizeOfHeaders.title: Size of Headers
SizeOfHeaders.description: The combined size of the DOS stub, PE header, and section headers.
SizeOfHeaders.security_notes: Unusual header sizes might indicate header manipulation or corruption.

CheckSum.title: CheckSum
CheckSum.description: A checksum value for the image. This field is used for integrity verification.
CheckSum.security_notes: Non-zero checksums should be validated. Zero is normal for many files.

Subsystem.title: Subsystem
Subsystem.description: Specifies the Windows subsystem that will run this executable: 2 (Windows GUI), 3 (Windows CUI), 1 (Native), 5 (OS/2 CUI).
Subsystem.purpose: Determine how Windows should handle the application
Subsystem.security_notes: Native subsystem (1) in user-mode executables is suspicious - indicates kernel-mode code running in user space. Could be rootkit or privilege escalation attempt.

DllCharacteristics.title: DLL Characteristics
DllCharacteristics.description: 16-bit bitmask in the optional header (PE spec). Official values: 0x0020 High entropy VA (64-bit ASLR space), 0x0040 Dynamic base (ASLR), 0x0080 Force integrity, 0x0100 NX compatible (DEP), 0x0200 No isolation, 0x0400 No SEH, 0x0800 No bind, 0x1000 AppContainer, 0x2000 WDM driver, 0x4000 Control Flow Guard (CFG), 0x8000 Terminal server aware. The Meaning column and the “This image” box list which of these are set in the opened file.
DllCharacteristics.purpose: Define DLL behavior and security features for the Windows loader
DllCharacteristics.security_notes: Missing NX or CFG on modern binaries can weaken exploit resistance. Compare the decoded list with what you expect from the toolchain.

SizeOfStackReserve.title: Size of Stack Reserve
SizeOfStackReserve.description: The size of the stack to reserve in virtual memory. This is the maximum stack size the process can use.
SizeOfStackReserve.security_notes: Very large stack reserves might indicate stack overflow attacks or memory exhaustion attempts.

SizeOfStackCommit.title: Size of Stack Commit
SizeOfStackCommit.description: The size of the stack to commit in virtual memory. This is the initial stack size that is actually allocated.
SizeOfStackCommit.security_notes: Unusual stack commit sizes might indicate manipulation or optimization attempts.

SizeOfHeapReserve.title: Size of Heap Reserve
SizeOfHeapReserve.description: The size of the local heap to reserve in virtual memory. This is the maximum heap size the process can use.
SizeOfHeapReserve.security_notes: Very large heap reserves might indicate memory exhaustion attacks or manipulation.

SizeOfHeapCommit.title: Size of Heap Commit
SizeOfHeapCommit.description: The size of the local heap to commit in virtual memory. This is the initial heap size that is actually allocated.
SizeOfHeapCommit.security_notes: Unusual heap commit sizes might indicate manipulation or optimization attempts.

LoaderFlags.title: Loader Flags
LoaderFlags.description: Flags that control the loader behavior: 0x0001 (Break on load), 0x0002 (Debug on load), 0x0004 (Default break on load), 0x0008 (Default debug on load), 0x0010 (Incremental link), 0x0020 (Suppress incremental link), 0x0040 (Safe SEH handler), 0x0080 (Guard CF), 0x0100 (Terminal server aware).
LoaderFlags.security_notes: Debug flags enabled in release builds are suspicious. Missing security flags might indicate vulnerable code.

NumberOfRvaAndSizes.title: Number of RVA and Sizes
NumberOfRvaAndSizes.description: The number of data directory entries that follow. This should always be 16 for standard PE files.
NumberOfRvaAndSizes.purpose: Define the number of data directories
NumberOfRvaAndSizes.security_notes: Values other than 16 might indicate file corruption or non-standard PE format.

Name.title: Section Name
Name.description: An 8-character name that identifies the section. Common names include .text (code), .data (data), .rdata (read-only data), .idata (imports), .edata (exports), .rsrc (resources), .reloc (relocations).
Name.security_notes: Suspicious section names: UPX0/UPX1 (packed), .aspack, .vmp0 (VMProtect), .themida. Unusual names might indicate obfuscation or malware.

SectionName.title: Section Name
SectionName.description: An 8-character name that identifies the section. Common names include .text (code), .data (data), .rdata (read-only data), .idata (imports), .edata (exports), .rsrc (resources), .reloc (relocations).
SectionName.security_notes: Suspicious section names: UPX0/UPX1 (packed), .aspack, .vmp0 (VMProtect), .themida. Unusual names might indicate obfuscation or malware.

Export Directory.title: Export Directory
Export Directory.description: Contains information about functions and data that the module exports for use by other modules. This directory points to the export address table (EAT) which lists all exported symbols.
Export Directory.purpose: Enable other modules to import functions and data from this executable
Export Directory.security_notes: Critical for malware triage – look for exported functions with purely ordinal names, duplicate names, or exports that proxy straight into system DLLs (common in DLL sideloading). Unexpected exports (especially networking, process injection, or service routines) can indicate command-and-control or persistence hooks.

Import Directory.title: Import Directory
Import Directory.description: Lists all modules and functions that this executable imports from other modules. Each import entry specifies the module name and the functions being imported.
Import Directory.purpose: Resolve dependencies on external functions and libraries at runtime
Import Directory.security_notes: Review imported DLLs and APIs for suspicious behavior: direct imports of functions such as WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread, VirtualAllocEx, Nt* syscalls, or unusual DLLs (e.g. dbghelp, samsrv, wininet) often reveal the malware’s capabilities. Sparse imports combined with a high entry point entropy usually suggest packed or dynamically resolved APIs.

Resource Directory.title: Resource Directory
Resource Directory.description: Contains application resources such as icons, bitmaps, strings, and version information. Resources are organized in a hierarchical structure.
Resource Directory.purpose: Store application resources and assets for runtime use
Resource Directory.security_notes: Check for hidden resources, suspicious embedded content, or resources that might contain malicious code

Exception Directory.title: Exception Directory
Exception Directory.description: Contains exception handling information for the executable. This directory is used by the Windows Structured Exception Handling (SEH) mechanism.
Exception Directory.purpose: Handle runtime exceptions and errors gracefully
Exception Directory.security_notes: Check for exception handlers that might be used for anti-debugging or code injection techniques

Certificate Directory.title: Certificate Directory
Certificate Directory.description: Contains digital signature information and certificates for code signing. This verifies the authenticity and integrity of the executable.
Certificate Directory.purpose: Verify the identity of the software publisher and ensure code hasn't been tampered with
Certificate Directory.security_notes: Critical for security - unsigned executables or invalid certificates may indicate malicious software

Base Relocation Directory.title: Base Relocation Directory
Base Relocation Directory.description: Contains relocation information for when the executable needs to be loaded at a different base address than its preferred base.
Base Relocation Directory.purpose: Enable the loader to relocate the executable to different memory addresses if needed
Base Relocation Directory.security_notes: Check for excessive relocations that might indicate ASLR bypass attempts or suspicious loading behavior

Debug Directory.title: Debug Directory
Debug Directory.description: Contains debug information such as line numbers, symbol tables, and other debugging data. This information is used by debuggers and development tools.
Debug Directory.purpose: Provide debugging information for development and troubleshooting
Debug Directory.security_notes: Debug information can reveal internal structure - its presence or absence might indicate obfuscation or stripping

Architecture Directory.title: Architecture Directory
Architecture Directory.description: Contains architecture-specific data and information. This directory is used for specialized architectures or extended features.
Architecture Directory.security_notes: Check for unexpected architecture data that might indicate cross-compilation or suspicious modifications

Global Pointer Directory.title: Global Pointer Directory
Global Pointer Directory.description: Contains information about global pointers used by the executable. This is primarily used in RISC architectures.
Global Pointer Directory.purpose: Manage global pointer references for efficient memory access
Global Pointer Directory.security_notes: Unusual global pointer usage might indicate suspicious memory access patterns

TLS Directory.title: TLS Directory
TLS Directory.description: Contains Thread Local Storage information. TLS allows each thread to have its own copy of certain variables.
TLS Directory.purpose: Provide thread-specific storage for multi-threaded applications
TLS Directory.security_notes: Check for TLS callbacks that might be used for anti-debugging or initialization of malicious code

Load Configuration Directory.title: Load Configuration Directory
Load Configuration Directory.description: Contains configuration information for how the executable should be loaded, including security features like Control Flow Guard and SEHOP.
Load Configuration Directory.purpose: Configure security features and loading behavior
Load Configuration Directory.security_notes: Critical for security analysis - check for disabled security features that might indicate malicious intent

Exc RuntimeFunctionCount.title: Estimated runtime function entries
Exc RuntimeFunctionCount.description: For x64 images the Exception Directory is usually an array of IMAGE_RUNTIME_FUNCTION entries (12 bytes each: begin RVA, end RVA, unwind info RVA). Dividing the directory size by 12 estimates how many functions publish unwind data for x64 exception handling.
Exc RuntimeFunctionCount.purpose: Orient analysis of stack unwinding / reversed execution flow
Exc RuntimeFunctionCount.note: ARM64 and other architectures use different entry layouts—see architecture-specific PE documentation.
Exc RuntimeFunctionCount.security_notes: Malware may alter or strip exception tables; very low counts in large modules can be suspicious.

Exc First BeginRVA.title: First RUNTIME_FUNCTION.BeginAddress
Exc First BeginRVA.description: RVA of the first byte of the first function that has an associated unwind/exception record in this table.
Exc First BeginRVA.purpose: Anchor into the exception directory blob when learning the format
Exc First BeginRVA.security_notes: Compare against code sections; mismatches can hint at hand-crafted tables.

Exc First EndRVA.title: First RUNTIME_FUNCTION.EndAddress
Exc First EndRVA.description: RVA just past the last byte of the first function region described by the entry.
Exc First EndRVA.purpose: Define the RVA span covered by the unwind metadata
Exc First EndRVA.security_notes: End before begin or spans outside executable sections warrant a closer look.

Exc First UnwindRVA.title: First RUNTIME_FUNCTION.UnwindData / UnwindInfoAddress
Exc First UnwindRVA.description: Points to unwind info (x64: UNWIND_INFO structures) that tell the OS how to walk stack frames for this function.
Exc First UnwindRVA.purpose: Link each function range to its unwind metadata
Exc First UnwindRVA.security_notes: Unwind chains are occasionally abused for obfuscation; verify the target lies in a valid section.

Exc Note.title: Exception directory note
Exc Note.description: PEHint currently expands the classic x64 three-DWORD RUNTIME_FUNCTION row in the tree. Other machine types may use packed ARM64 records or legacy x86 SEH chains instead.
Exc Note.purpose: Set expectations when browsing non-x64 binaries
Exc Note.security_notes: Always confirm architecture from the PE Header Machine field before interpreting this directory.

TLS StartOfRawData.title: TLS StartAddressOfRawData
TLS StartOfRawData.description: Virtual address where the template for thread-local initialized data begins—the loader copies from this range when creating TLS storage.
TLS StartOfRawData.purpose: Locate TLS template bytes in the image
TLS StartOfRawData.security_notes: TLS callbacks run early during process init; malware sometimes hides code behind TLS directories.

TLS EndOfRawData.title: TLS EndAddressOfRawData
TLS EndOfRawData.description: Virtual address marking the end of the TLS template region (exclusive, per Microsoft convention).
TLS EndOfRawData.purpose: Bound the TLS template for validation
TLS EndOfRawData.security_notes: Implausible span sizes may indicate corruption or tampering.

TLS AddressOfIndex.title: TLS AddressOfIndex
TLS AddressOfIndex.description: Address of the TLS slot index variable the loader updates so the runtime can find each thread's TLS block.
TLS AddressOfIndex.security_notes: Useful when correlating disassembly with thread-local accesses.

TLS AddressOfCallBacks.title: TLS AddressOfCallBacks
TLS AddressOfCallBacks.description: Pointer to an array of TLS callback RVAs (null-terminated). Callbacks run before the normal entry point.
TLS AddressOfCallBacks.purpose: Run per-process initialization tied to TLS setup
TLS AddressOfCallBacks.security_notes: Extra callbacks or callbacks pointing into odd sections are a common packer / anti-analysis signal.

TLS SizeOfZeroFill.title: TLS SizeOfZeroFill
TLS SizeOfZeroFill.description: Extra byte count of TLS storage that should be zero-initialized beyond the templated region.
TLS SizeOfZeroFill.security_notes: Very large values can hint at suspicious allocations.

TLS Characteristics.title: TLS Characteristics
TLS Characteristics.description: Reserved flags for future TLS features; usually zero in modern binaries.
TLS Characteristics.purpose: Forward compatibility for the TLS directory
TLS Characteristics.security_notes: Non-zero unexpected bits deserve documentation-level verification.

LoadCfg StructureSize.title: Load Config Size
LoadCfg StructureSize.description: Self-reported byte length of the IMAGE_LOAD_CONFIG_DIRECTORY variant actually present in the image. Larger sizes include optional tail fields (e.g., Control Flow Guard metadata) introduced in newer Visual Studio toolchains.
LoadCfg StructureSize.purpose: Version the load configuration block and know how much follows
LoadCfg StructureSize.security_notes: Size smaller than claimed fields means the PE is inconsistent or truncated—treat guard flags skeptically.

LoadCfg TimeDateStamp.title: Load Config TimeDateStamp
LoadCfg TimeDateStamp.description: Optional timestamp associated with the load configuration block (often mirrors the link time of the toolchain that produced the structure).
LoadCfg TimeDateStamp.purpose: Correlate security mitigations with build era
LoadCfg TimeDateStamp.security_notes: Mismatch with the PE header timestamp is not inherently malicious but can indicate post-link edits.

LoadCfg MajorVersion.title: Load Config MajorVersion
LoadCfg MajorVersion.description: Major version of the load configuration structure layout understood by the linker.
LoadCfg MajorVersion.purpose: Infer which optional tail fields may exist
LoadCfg MajorVersion.security_notes: Pairs with MinorVersion; consult Microsoft docs for exact sizes per version.

LoadCfg MinorVersion.title: Load Config MinorVersion
LoadCfg MinorVersion.description: Minor version of the load configuration structure layout.
LoadCfg MinorVersion.security_notes: Newer minors add mitigations (e.g., EH continuation, retpoline metadata) beyond the base struct.

LoadCfg SecurityCookie.title: SecurityCookie pointer
LoadCfg SecurityCookie.description: For PE32 this is typically an RVA to the stack cookie used by /GS; for PE32+ it is the VA of that cookie. The runtime XORs it to detect stack buffer overflows.
LoadCfg SecurityCookie.security_notes: Stripped or duplicated cookies weaken protections—common in deliberately unsafe builds or obfuscated samples.

LoadCfg SEHandlerTable.title: SE Handler Table
LoadCfg SEHandlerTable.description: Pointer (RVA on 32-bit, VA on 64-bit) to the SafeSEH handler table when SafeSEH mitigations are enabled.
LoadCfg SEHandlerTable.purpose: Restrict which exception handlers may run on 32-bit images
LoadCfg SEHandlerTable.security_notes: Absence on 32-bit binaries with many SEH records can hint at older toolchains or tampering.

LoadCfg SEHandlerCount.title: SE Handler Count
LoadCfg SEHandlerCount.description: Number of entries described by the SafeSEH table (when present).
LoadCfg SEHandlerCount.security_notes: Huge counts in tiny programs may indicate malformed metadata.

LoadCfg GuardCFCheckFunction.title: Guard CF check function pointer
LoadCfg GuardCFCheckFunction.description: Address of the compiler-generated Control Flow Guard validation stub invoked before indirect calls.
LoadCfg GuardCFCheckFunction.purpose: Enforce indirect call targets at runtime on CFG-enabled systems
LoadCfg GuardCFCheckFunction.security_notes: Zero when /guard:cf is off; repointing this value is a common exploitation target.

LoadCfg GuardCFDispatchFunction.title: Guard CF dispatch function pointer
LoadCfg GuardCFDispatchFunction.description: Helper used by the loader/runtime for CFG dispatch paths (implementation detail of MSVC mitigations).
LoadCfg GuardCFDispatchFunction.purpose: Wire CFG bookkeeping together with the check stub
LoadCfg GuardCFDispatchFunction.security_notes: Should reside in trusted system or module code—unexpected modules warrant investigation.

LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionTable.title: Guard CF function table
LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionTable.description: Pointer to the bitmap/table describing valid indirect-call targets for Control Flow Guard.
LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionTable.purpose: Tell the kernel which call sites are legitimate when mitigation is active
LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionTable.security_notes: Manipulating this table can widen ROP gadgets—compare against known-good baselines.

LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionCount.title: Guard CF function count
LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionCount.description: Companion counter for entries encoded in the CFG function table—exact interpretation depends on toolchain version.
LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionCount.purpose: Relate table size to image complexity
LoadCfg GuardCFFunctionCount.security_notes: Zero with instrumentation flags set can indicate a broken or hand-built PE.

LoadCfg GuardFlags.title: GuardFlags bitmask
LoadCfg GuardFlags.description: Bitfield describing which mitigations accompany the load config tail—common bits include CF_INSTRUMENTED, CF_FUNCTION_TABLE_PRESENT, RF_INSTRUMENTED (Return Flow Guard / related features), and export-suppression helpers.
LoadCfg GuardFlags.purpose: Summarize modern exploit mitigations baked into the image
LoadCfg GuardFlags.security_notes: Missing CFG bits on newer Microsoft binaries is unusual; malware may strip mitigations to simplify exploitation.

Res Characteristics.title: Resource directory Characteristics
Res Characteristics.description: First dword of the root IMAGE_RESOURCE_DIRECTORY. Usually zero; reserved in the PE specification for future use.
Res Characteristics.purpose: Reserved field at the start of the resource tree header
Res Characteristics.security_notes: Non-zero values are rare—verify the file is not hand-crafted or corrupted.

Res TimeDateStamp.title: Resource directory TimeDateStamp
Res TimeDateStamp.description: Unix-style time stamp for when the resource data was built, if the toolchain filled it in. Often zero in practice.
Res TimeDateStamp.purpose: Optional build-time metadata for the resource section
Res TimeDateStamp.security_notes: Mismatches with other timestamps can hint at post-build resource injection.

Res MajorVersion.title: Resource major version
Res MajorVersion.description: Major version number associated with the resource directory header (toolchain-specific; often zero).
Res MajorVersion.security_notes: Unusual values alone are rarely actionable—combine with other anomalies.

Res MinorVersion.title: Resource minor version
Res MinorVersion.description: Minor version number paired with Res MajorVersion (often zero).

Res NumberOfNamedEntries.title: NumberOfNamedEntries
Res NumberOfNamedEntries.description: Count of directory entries that use string names (high bit set in the name field). These appear before ID entries in the entry array.
Res NumberOfNamedEntries.purpose: Tell the loader how many named entries follow the header
Res NumberOfNamedEntries.security_notes: Named entries at the type level are less common than numeric RT_* types; large counts may warrant manual inspection.

Res NumberOfIdEntries.title: NumberOfIdEntries
Res NumberOfIdEntries.description: Count of directory entries identified by numeric ID (e.g. RT_MANIFEST=24, RT_VERSION=16). Listed after named entries.
Res NumberOfIdEntries.purpose: Enumerate resource types or next-level IDs in the tree
Res NumberOfIdEntries.security_notes: Missing expected types (e.g. no manifest on a GUI app) can be a packaging choice or tampering signal in context.

Res TypeId.title: Resource type ID (first level)
Res TypeId.description: Numeric resource type at the root directory level. Well-known values include RT_ICON (3), RT_DIALOG (5), RT_MANIFEST (24), RT_VERSION (16). PEHint labels common RT_* names when recognized.
Res TypeId.purpose: Identify which resource branch (icons, dialogs, manifest XML, etc.) this entry describes
Res TypeId.security_notes: RT_MANIFEST holds application/dll manifest XML used for UAC, DPI, and side-by-side—inspect embedded content for unexpected elevation or dependency tricks.

Manifest DataRVA.title: Embedded manifest RVA
Manifest DataRVA.description: Relative virtual address of the raw bytes of the RT_MANIFEST resource (typically UTF-8 XML). PEHint locates the first manifest leaf under type 24 when present.
Manifest DataRVA.purpose: Let the loader read the Win32 side-by-side / compatibility manifest
Manifest DataRVA.security_notes: Manifests can request administrator rights, declare dependencies, or influence DLL search—compare with expected application behavior.

Manifest Size.title: Embedded manifest size
Manifest Size.description: Size in bytes of the manifest resource blob at Manifest DataRVA.
Manifest Size.purpose: Bound the manifest for mapping and validation
Manifest Size.security_notes: Very small or huge sizes relative to peers can indicate truncation or appended content—verify with a hex view.

Manifest Preview.title: Manifest text preview
Manifest Preview.description: Short UTF-8 preview of the manifest XML (truncated for display). Full content is in the mapped section at the manifest RVA.
Manifest Preview.purpose: Quickly spot requestedExecutionLevel, dependency assemblies, or dpiAware settings
Manifest Preview.security_notes: Do not rely on the preview alone for compliance—export or open the full resource for auditing.

CLR cb (reported).title: CLR header size (truncated image)
CLR cb (reported).description: The cb field read from IMAGE_COR20_HEADER when the on-disk directory region is smaller than a full COR20 header. Indicates the structure is incomplete or the image is truncated.
CLR cb (reported).purpose: Report how many bytes the image claims for the COM+ descriptor
CLR cb (reported).security_notes: Broken .NET headers can appear in corrupted downloads or intentional anti-analysis—compare with a known-good build.

CLR cb.title: CLR header size (bytes)
CLR cb.description: Size in bytes of the CLR/COM+ header structure (IMAGE_COR20_HEADER), including fields actually present in the image.
CLR cb.purpose: Version and extend the CLI descriptor consistently across runtimes
CLR cb.security_notes: cb smaller than expected for the runtime version can indicate tampering or stripped metadata.

CLR MajorRuntimeVersion.title: CLR major runtime version
CLR MajorRuntimeVersion.description: Major version of the CLR runtime the image targets (paired with MinorRuntimeVersion).
CLR MajorRuntimeVersion.purpose: Help the loader pick compatible CLR behavior
CLR MajorRuntimeVersion.security_notes: Mismatches with metadata version or unusual pairings can flag mixed or repacked assemblies.

CLR MinorRuntimeVersion.title: CLR minor runtime version
CLR MinorRuntimeVersion.description: Minor version number paired with MajorRuntimeVersion for the CLI header.

CLR MetaData RVA.title: CLR metadata RVA
CLR MetaData RVA.description: Relative virtual address of the CLI metadata root (#~ stream, strings, etc.) described in ECMA-335.
CLR MetaData RVA.purpose: Locate tables for types, methods, resources, and assembly identity
CLR MetaData RVA.security_notes: Managed reverse engineering and signing analysis typically start here—metadata RVA 0 with ILONLY set is suspicious.

CLR MetaData Size.title: CLR metadata size
CLR MetaData Size.description: Size in bytes of the metadata blob referenced by CLR MetaData RVA.
CLR MetaData Size.security_notes: Tiny or zero size with non-zero RVA often indicates a broken or crafted file.

CLR Flags.title: CLR COM+ flags
CLR Flags.description: Bitfield for COMIMAGE_FLAGS (e.g. ILONLY, 32BITREQUIRED, STRONGNAMESIGNED, TRACKDEBUGDATA). Decoded in the Meaning column when recognized.
CLR Flags.purpose: Declare whether the module is pure IL, requires 32-bit, is strong-named, etc.
CLR Flags.security_notes: Strong-name and IL-only flags affect trust and loading—verify with signing tools if security decisions depend on them.

CLR EntryPointToken.title: CLR entry point token / RVA
CLR EntryPointToken.description: If ILONLY: metadata token for the managed entry method; otherwise may be an RVA to a native stub. Interpretation follows the flag bits.
CLR EntryPointToken.purpose: Tell the CLR where execution begins
CLR EntryPointToken.security_notes: Unexpected tokens or RVAs can point to obfuscated or native interop entry points.

CLR Resources RVA.title: CLR managed resources RVA
CLR Resources RVA.description: RVA of embedded .NET resources (not the Win32 RT_RCDATA tree—this is the managed resource section).
CLR Resources RVA.purpose: Load localized strings, images, and other embedded assets for the assembly
CLR Resources RVA.security_notes: Large resource blobs can hide payloads—scan with appropriate .NET tools.

CLR Resources Size.title: CLR managed resources size
CLR Resources Size.description: Size of the managed resource block referenced by CLR Resources RVA.
CLR Resources Size.purpose: Bound managed resources in the image

CLR StrongNameSignature RVA.title: Strong name signature RVA
CLR StrongNameSignature RVA.description: RVA of the strong-name signature blob used when the assembly is signed (hash over the image).
CLR StrongNameSignature RVA.purpose: Support integrity and identity for strongly named assemblies
CLR StrongNameSignature RVA.security_notes: Present signature with STRONGNAMESIGNED flag cleared (or vice versa) deserves verification.

CLR StrongNameSignature Size.title: Strong name signature size
CLR StrongNameSignature Size.description: Size of the strong-name signature data.

CLR CodeManagerTable RVA.title: Code manager table RVA
CLR CodeManagerTable RVA.description: Historical/optional table for CLR code managers; often zero in modern images.
CLR CodeManagerTable RVA.security_notes: Non-zero values are uncommon—verify against tooling expectations.

CLR CodeManagerTable Size.title: Code manager table size
CLR CodeManagerTable Size.description: Size of the code manager table.

CLR VTableFixups RVA.title: VTable fixups RVA
CLR VTableFixups RVA.description: RVA of VTable fixup records for C++/CLI and interop scenarios.
CLR VTableFixups RVA.purpose: Patch vtables when loading mixed-mode images
CLR VTableFixups RVA.security_notes: Relevant mainly for mixed assemblies—unexpected fixups may indicate interop surface area.

CLR VTableFixups Size.title: VTable fixups size
CLR VTableFixups Size.description: Size of the VTable fixup array.

CLR ExportAddressTableJumps RVA.title: Export address table jumps RVA
CLR ExportAddressTableJumps RVA.description: RVA of jump thunks related to exported managed methods in some scenarios (often unused).
CLR ExportAddressTableJumps RVA.purpose: Support CLR export forwarding edge cases
CLR ExportAddressTableJumps RVA.security_notes: Rarely populated—non-zero values merit context from the compiler toolchain.

CLR ExportAddressTableJumps Size.title: Export address table jumps size
CLR ExportAddressTableJumps Size.description: Size of the export jump table.

CLR ManagedNativeHeader RVA.title: Managed native header RVA
CLR ManagedNativeHeader RVA.description: RVA of the COR20 managed native header (NGEN/ReadyToRun style data) when present.
CLR ManagedNativeHeader RVA.purpose: Support precompiled native code for managed assemblies
CLR ManagedNativeHeader RVA.security_notes: Presence indicates native image optimization—analysis may differ from pure IL.

CLR ManagedNativeHeader Size.title: Managed native header size
CLR ManagedNativeHeader Size.description: Size of the managed native header block.

Bound Import Directory.title: Bound Import Directory
Bound Import Directory.description: Contains pre-bound import information that can speed up loading by avoiding runtime import resolution.
Bound Import Directory.purpose: Optimize loading performance by pre-binding imports
Bound Import Directory.security_notes: Check for bound imports that might be used to hide suspicious import behavior

Import Address Table Directory.title: Import Address Table Directory
Import Address Table Directory.description: Contains the Import Address Table (IAT) which stores the actual addresses of imported functions after they are resolved at runtime.
Import Address Table Directory.purpose: Store resolved addresses of imported functions for efficient calling
Import Address Table Directory.security_notes: Check for IAT hooking or suspicious import resolution that might indicate code injection

Delay Import Directory.title: Delay Import Directory
Delay Import Directory.description: Contains information about functions that are imported but not resolved until they are first called. This can improve startup performance.
Delay Import Directory.purpose: Defer import resolution until functions are actually needed
Delay Import Directory.security_notes: Check for delayed imports that might be used to hide suspicious behavior until runtime

COM+ Runtime Header Directory.title: COM+ Runtime Header Directory
COM+ Runtime Header Directory.description: Contains COM+ runtime information and metadata. This directory is used by COM+ applications and services.
COM+ Runtime Header Directory.purpose: Provide COM+ runtime support and metadata for COM+ applications
COM+ Runtime Header Directory.security_notes: Check for COM+ runtime data that might be used for COM hijacking or suspicious COM object creation

Reserved.title: Reserved Directory
Reserved.description: Reserved for future use by Microsoft. This directory entry is not currently used but may be defined in future Windows versions.
Reserved.purpose: Reserved for future Windows features and extensions
Reserved.security_notes: Check for any data in reserved directories as this might indicate experimental or suspicious features

VirtualSize.title: Virtual Size
VirtualSize.description: The size of the section when loaded into memory. This may be different from the raw data size due to alignment requirements and padding.
VirtualSize.security_notes: Suspicious if virtual size >> raw size - could indicate unpacking or code injection. Very large virtual sizes might be malware trying to allocate excessive memory.

VirtualAddress.title: Virtual Address
VirtualAddress.description: The relative virtual address (RVA) where this section will be loaded in memory. This is relative to the image base address.
VirtualAddress.purpose: Define memory layout and section positioning
VirtualAddress.security_notes: Suspicious if virtual address is very low (<0x1000) or overlaps with other sections. Could indicate code injection or section manipulation.

SizeOfRawData.title: Size of Raw Data
SizeOfRawData.description: The actual size of the section data stored in the file. This represents the number of bytes that will be read from disk.
SizeOfRawData.note: Must be aligned to file alignment boundary
SizeOfRawData.security_notes: Suspicious if raw size is 0 but virtual size > 0 - indicates uninitialized data section that could be used for code injection. Very large raw sizes might indicate embedded malicious content.

PointerToRawData.title: Pointer to Raw Data
PointerToRawData.description: The file offset where the section's raw data begins. This tells the loader where to read the section data from disk.
PointerToRawData.purpose: Locate section data within the file
PointerToRawData.format: File offset from beginning of file
PointerToRawData.security_notes: Check for suspicious offsets pointing to overlay or very large values. Could indicate hidden malicious content or file manipulation.

PointerToRelocations.title: Pointer to Relocations
PointerToRelocations.description: Pointer to the relocation table for this section. This is typically 0 in modern PE files.
PointerToRelocations.security_notes: Non-zero values might indicate complex relocations or manipulation.

PointerToLinenumbers.title: Pointer to Line Numbers
PointerToLinenumbers.description: Pointer to the line number table for this section. This is typically 0 in release builds.
PointerToLinenumbers.security_notes: Non-zero values in release builds might indicate debug information left behind or manipulation.

NumberOfRelocations.title: Number of Relocations
NumberOfRelocations.description: The number of relocation entries for this section. Relocations are needed when the section cannot be loaded at its preferred virtual address.
NumberOfRelocations.note: Usually 0 for most sections in modern executables
NumberOfRelocations.security_notes: High number of relocations in unusual sections might indicate code injection or manipulation. Check if relocations point to suspicious addresses.

NumberOfLineNumbers.title: Number of Line Numbers
NumberOfLineNumbers.description: The number of line number entries for this section. These are used for debugging to map machine code back to source code.
NumberOfLineNumbers.security_notes: Line numbers in suspicious sections might help trace malware origin. Missing line numbers in code sections could indicate obfuscation.

SectionCharacteristics.title: Section Characteristics
SectionCharacteristics.description: Flags that define the section's properties and permissions. Common flags: 0x20 (contains code), 0x40 (contains initialized data), 0x80 (contains uninitialized data), 0x20000000 (executable), 0x80000000 (readable), 0x40000000 (writable).
SectionCharacteristics.security_notes: CRITICAL: Executable data sections (0x40 + 0x20000000) are highly suspicious - indicates code injection. Writable code sections (0x20 + 0x40000000) suggest self-modifying code or malware.

Section.title: PE Section
Section.description: A section in a Portable Executable file represents a logical division of the executable's content. Each section contains specific types of data (code, initialized data, resources, etc.) and has defined characteristics that determine how it's loaded into memory and what operations are allowed.
Section.purpose: Organize executable content into logical, loadable segments with specific permissions and attributes
Section.note: Common section names include .text (executable code), .data (initialized data), .rdata (read-only data), .rsrc (resources), .reloc (relocations), .idata (imports), and .edata (exports)
Section.security_notes: Critical for security analysis - check section characteristics for suspicious permissions (especially W+X combinations), look for hidden or obfuscated sections, verify section alignment, and examine unusual section names that might indicate packing or obfuscation.

VirtualAddress_DataDir.title: Data Directory RVA
VirtualAddress_DataDir.description: The relative virtual address (RVA) of the data directory entry.
VirtualAddress_DataDir.purpose: Locate data directory content in memory
VirtualAddress_DataDir.security_notes: Verify that RVA points to valid section content, not to overlay or invalid memory regions.

Size_DataDir.title: Data Directory Size
Size_DataDir.description: The size of the data directory entry in bytes.
Size_DataDir.security_notes: Unusual sizes might indicate data injection or manipulation.

OriginalFirstThunk.title: Original First Thunk
OriginalFirstThunk.description: RVA to the original thunk table containing function names and ordinals.
OriginalFirstThunk.security_notes: Manipulation of this field can hide imported functions or redirect imports.

TimeDateStamp_Import.title: Import Time/Date Stamp
TimeDateStamp_Import.description: Timestamp when the import was bound. 0 indicates not bound, -1 indicates bound.
TimeDateStamp_Import.security_notes: Unusual timestamps might indicate import manipulation or binding issues.

ForwarderChain.title: Forwarder Chain
ForwarderChain.description: Index into the forwarder chain. -1 if no forwarders.
ForwarderChain.security_notes: Complex forwarder chains might indicate obfuscation or redirection.

Name_Import.title: Import DLL Name
Name_Import.description: RVA to the name of the DLL being imported from.
Name_Import.security_notes: Check for suspicious DLL names or imports from non-standard locations.

FirstThunk.title: First Thunk
FirstThunk.description: RVA to the import address table (IAT) that will be filled with function addresses.
FirstThunk.security_notes: IAT manipulation is common in malware to hide imported functions.

Characteristics_Export.title: Export Characteristics
Characteristics_Export.security_notes: Non-zero values might indicate corruption or manipulation.

TimeDateStamp_Export.title: Export Time/Date Stamp
TimeDateStamp_Export.description: Timestamp when the export table was created.
TimeDateStamp_Export.security_notes: Unusual timestamps might indicate manipulation or fake exports.

MajorVersion_Export.title: Export Major Version
MajorVersion_Export.description: Major version number of the export table.
MajorVersion_Export.security_notes: Unusual version numbers might indicate manipulation.

MinorVersion_Export.title: Export Minor Version
MinorVersion_Export.description: Minor version number of the export table.
MinorVersion_Export.security_notes: Unusual version numbers might indicate manipulation.

Name_Export.title: Export Module Name
Name_Export.description: RVA to the name of the module that contains the exports.
Name_Export.security_notes: Verify module name matches expected values.

OrdinalBase.title: Ordinal Base
OrdinalBase.security_notes: Unusual ordinal bases might indicate manipulation.

NumberOfFunctions.title: Number of Functions
NumberOfFunctions.security_notes: Unusually large numbers might indicate code injection or fake exports.

NumberOfNames.title: Number of Names
NumberOfNames.description: Number of exported functions with names.
NumberOfNames.security_notes: Should match or be less than NumberOfFunctions.

AddressOfFunctions.title: Address of Functions
AddressOfFunctions.description: RVA to the array of function addresses.
AddressOfFunctions.security_notes: Verify addresses point to valid code sections.

AddressOfNames.title: Address of Names
AddressOfNames.description: RVA to the array of function name pointers.
AddressOfNames.security_notes: Verify names are valid and not suspicious.

AddressOfNameOrdinals.title: Address of Name Ordinals
AddressOfNameOrdinals.description: RVA to the array of ordinal numbers.
AddressOfNameOrdinals.security_notes: Verify ordinals are within valid range.

NT Headers.title: NT Headers
NT Headers.description: The NT Headers (also known as PE Headers) contain the core information about the Portable Executable file format. This section includes the PE signature, File Header, Optional Header, and Section Headers.
NT Headers.purpose: Provide the essential PE file structure information for the Windows loader
NT Headers.note: NT Headers structure: PE Signature (4 bytes) + File Header (20 bytes) + Optional Header (variable size) + Section Headers (40 bytes each)
NT Headers.security_notes: The NT Headers are critical for understanding the executable's structure. Malware often modifies these headers to hide malicious behavior or evade detection. Pay special attention to the EntryPoint, ImageBase, and DllCharacteristics fields in the Optional Header.

Export Directory RVA.title: Export Directory RVA
Export Directory RVA.description: The Relative Virtual Address (RVA) field specifies the virtual address where the Export Directory data structure begins in memory. RVA is an offset relative to the image base address.
Export Directory RVA.purpose: This field points to the location of the Export Directory structure within the loaded image. If the value is 0, the directory is not present in this PE file.
Export Directory RVA.note: RVA values are relative to the ImageBase. To convert to a file offset, you need to find which section contains this RVA and calculate: FileOffset = RVA - Section.VirtualAddress + Section.PointerToRawData
Export Directory RVA.security_notes: Verify that RVA points to valid section content, not to overlay or invalid memory regions.

Export Directory Size.title: Export Directory Size
Export Directory Size.description: The Size field specifies the size in bytes of the Export Directory structure.
Export Directory Size.purpose: This field indicates how many bytes the Export Directory occupies. Combined with the RVA field, it defines the complete memory range where the directory data is located.
Export Directory Size.note: If both RVA and Size are 0, the directory is not used in this PE file. The size is typically fixed for each directory type, but can vary for some directories like Resources.
Export Directory Size.security_notes: Unusual sizes might indicate data injection or manipulation.
